ta-01.note: 눈 means eye on your face (눈이 커요) and also snow falling from the sky (눈이 와요). Context tells the meaning.
배 means stomach (배가 아파요), the pear fruit (달콤한 배), or a ship on water (배를 타요).
다리 means a leg on your body (다리가 길어요) and also a bridge across water (다리를 건너요).

ta-02.note: 작다 means small in physical size (가방이 작아요), while 적다 means small in quantity or number (학생 수가 적어요). Do not mix them up.
빠르다 is an adjective meaning to be fast (비행기가 빨라요), while 빨리 is an adverb meaning quickly (빨리 오세요).
Opposites. 시작하다 means to begin an action (수업을 시작해요), while 끝나다 means to finish or end (영화가 끝나요).

ta-03.note: Both mean all or everyone. 다 is an everyday adverb (숙제를 다 했어요), while 모두 can be used as a noun or adverb (친구가 모두 왔어요).
Opposites. 많이 means a lot or much (밥을 많이 먹어요), while 조금 (or 좀) means a little (조금 기다리세요).
가장 means the most or best before adjectives (가장 좋아요), and also means the head of a family (우리 집의 가장).

ta-04.note: Both mean the most or best. 가장 is native Korean (가장 커요), while 제일 is Sino-Korean and very common in conversation (제일 좋아요).
Opposites. 높다 means high or tall (산이 높아요), while 낮다 means low (책상이 낮아요).
만 is the number ten thousand (만 원), and also a particle meaning only attached to nouns (물만 마셔요).

ta-05.note: 약 means medicine (약을 먹어요), and also means approximately or about before numbers (약 10분 걸려요).
반 means half (한 시 반, 반 개), and also means a class group at school (우리 반 친구).
셋 is the native number three used with counters (사과 세 개), while 삼 is the Sino-Korean number used for dates and minutes (3월, 삼십 분).

ta-06.note: 열 is the native Korean number ten (열 명), and also means a fever or body heat (열이 나요).
안 means inside (가방 안), and also the negative word not placed before verbs (안 가요, 안 먹어요).
셋 changes to 세 before a counter or noun (세 살, 세 개). Use 셋 when counting numbers by themselves (하나, 둘, 셋).

ta-07.note: Both mean birthday. 생일 is the standard everyday word (친구 생일), while 생신 is the honorific word used for elders (할머니 생신).
Opposites. 앞 means front (학교 앞), while 뒤 means behind or back (집 뒤). They also describe time order (앞으로 vs 뒤에).
Opposites. 가깝다 means near or close (역에서 가까워요), while 멀다 means far away (회사가 멀어요).

ta-08.note: Korean uses different verbs for clothes. 입다 is for body garments like shirts and pants (옷을 입어요), while 신다 is for footwear on feet (신발을 신어요).
Both are shoes. 구두 refers to dress shoes or formal leather shoes (구두를 신어요), while 운동화 refers to sneakers or sports shoes (운동화를 신어요).
원 is the currency unit of Korea (천 원), and also means a geometric circle (동그란 원).

ta-09.note: Both mean to sleep. 자다 is the standard verb (동생이 자요), while 주무시다 is the respectful honorific verb for elders (부모님이 주무세요).
빌리다 means to borrow from someone (도서관에서 책을 빌려요), while 빌려주다 means to lend to someone (친구에게 우산을 빌려줘요).
들다 has several common uses: to hold or carry in hand (가방을 들어요), or to like (마음에 들어요), or to cost money (돈이 들어요).

ta-10.note: 다녀오다 means to go somewhere and come back (학교에 다녀왔어요), while 돌아오다 emphasizes returning back to the starting place (집으로 돌아와요).
걷다 means to walk on foot (공원을 걸어요), and also to roll up sleeves or collect laundry (빨래를 걷어요).
Both mean a meal. 밥 is the everyday Korean word (밥을 먹어요), while 식사 is the formal Sino-Korean word (맛있게 식사하세요).

ta-11.note: Opposites. 사다 means to buy (가방을 사요), while 팔다 means to sell (가게에서 옷을 팔아요).
Opposites. 비싸다 means expensive (옷이 비싸요), while 싸다 means cheap or inexpensive (사과가 싸요).
시장 means a public market to shop (전통 시장에 가요), and also means the mayor of a city (서울 시장).

ta-12.note: 싸다 means to be cheap in price (과일이 싸요), and also means to pack or wrap items (가방에 짐을 싸요).
Both mean price. 값 is everyday native Korean (옷 값이 비싸요), while 가격 is formal (가격을 확인해요).
Opposites. 오늘 means today (오늘 만나요), while 내일 means tomorrow (내일 학교에 가요).

ta-13.note: 시 tells the clock hour (두 시예요 = it is 2 o'clock), while 시간 tells duration of time (두 시간 공부해요 = study for 2 hours).
Opposites. 전 means before or ago (한 시간 전에), while 후 means after or later (식사 후에).
때 means time or occasion (점심때, 방학 때), and also means dirt or grime on the skin (때를 밀어요).

ta-14.note: 밤 means nighttime (밤에 자요) and also a chestnut nut (맛있는 밤을 먹어요). Same pronunciation and spelling.
달 means the moon in the sky (달이 밝아요) and also a calendar month (한 달 동안 쉬어요).
Opposites. 먼저 means first or ahead (먼저 가세요), while 나중 means later or afterward (나중에 봐요).

ta-15.note: Opposites. 낮 means daytime (낮에는 따뜻해요), while 밤 means nighttime (밤에는 추워요).
아직 means still or not yet (아직 안 왔어요), while 벌써 means already (벌써 열두 시예요).
Opposites. 시작 means beginning or start (시작이 중요해요), while 끝 means end or finish (끝까지 들어요).

ta-16.note: 작년 means last year (작년에 한국에 왔어요), while 내년 means next year (내년에 졸업해요).
Both mean a moment or short while. 잠깐 is everyday and common (잠깐만 기다려요), while 잠시 is more formal (잠시 후 만나요).
중 means in the middle of an action (수업 중, 통화 중), and also historically a Buddhist monk (절의 스님).

ta-17.note: Opposites. 덥다 means hot weather (여름에는 더워요), while 춥다 means cold weather (겨울에는 추워요).
비 means rain falling from the sky (비가 와요), and also a broom for sweeping (빗자루와 비).
바람 means wind or breeze (바람이 불어요), and also a hope or wish (건강이 저의 바람이에요).

ta-18.note: 좋다 is an adjective taking 이/가 (음악이 좋아요), while 좋아하다 is an active verb taking 을/를 (음악을 좋아해요).
Opposites. 웃다 means to smile or laugh (환하게 웃어요), while 울다 means to weep or cry (슬퍼서 울어요).
Opposites. 재미있다 means fun or interesting (영화가 재미있어요), while 재미없다 means boring (책이 재미없어요).

ta-19.note: Opposites. 기쁘다 means glad or happy (선물을 받아서 기뻐요), while 슬프다 means sad (친구가 떠나서 슬퍼요).
싫다 is an adjective taking 이/가 (추위가 싫어요), while 싫어하다 is an active verb taking 을/를 (추위를 싫어해요).
만들다 means to make anything (옷을 만들어요), while 요리하다 specifically means to prepare and cook food (저녁을 요리해요).

ta-20.note: Both mean to eat. 먹다 is standard (사과를 먹어요), while 드시다 is the polite honorific verb for elders (할머니께서 진지를 드세요).
감 means the sweet persimmon fruit (맛있는 감을 먹어요), and also a feeling or sense (감이 좋아요).
Both mean a meal or cooked rice. 밥 is standard (밥을 먹어요), while 진지 is the respectful honorific word for elders (진지 드셨어요?).

ta-21.note: Both are polite honorific verbs for 먹다. 드시다 is widely used (맛있게 드세요), while 잡수시다 is an older traditional honorific for elders (할머니께서 진지를 잡수셨어요).
Both mean cup. 잔 is used as a counter for cups or glasses of drinks (물 한 잔, 커피 두 잔), while 컵 refers to the cup object itself (종이 컵).
술 means alcoholic beverage (술을 마셔요), and also a spoonful of food (밥 한 술).

ta-22.note: 사과 means the sweet apple fruit (사과를 먹어요) and also an apology (친구에게 사과해요). Same spelling and sound.
Both mean to order food. 시키다 is very common in everyday spoken Korean (피자를 시켜요), while 주문하다 is slightly more formal (메뉴를 주문해요).
Opposites. 맛있다 means delicious or tasty (불고기가 맛있어요), while 맛없다 means not delicious (음식이 맛없어요).

ta-23.note: 짜다 means salty in taste (음식이 짜요), and also means to squeeze out liquid or make a plan (치약을 짜요, 계획을 짜요).
Both mean to give. 주다 is standard (친구에게 책을 줘요), while 드리다 is the polite honorific used for elders (선생님께 선물을 드려요).
Opposites. 가다 means to go away (학교에 가요), while 오다 means to come toward the speaker (집에 와요).

ta-24.note: Both mean I or me. 나 is casual used with friends (나는 학생이야), while 저 is humble and polite (저는 학생이에요).
이 means this near the speaker (이 책), a tooth in the mouth (이가 아파요), and the Sino-Korean number two.
거기 refers to a location near the listener (거기 어디예요?), while 저기 refers to a place far from both speaker and listener (저기 건물이 보여요).

ta-25.note: 무슨 means what or what kind of (무슨 영화를 봐요?), while 어느 means which one among choices (어느 것을 골라요?).
Opposites. 켜다 means to turn on a light or machine (불을 켜요), while 끄다 means to turn it off (컴퓨터를 꺼요).
Opposites. 깨끗하다 means clean (방이 깨끗해요), while 더럽다 means dirty (신발이 더러워요).

ta-26.note: Both mean house or home. 집 is standard (우리 집), while 댁 is the honorific noun for an elder's home (선생님 댁).
Opposites. 넓다 means spacious or wide (방이 넓어요), while 좁다 means cramped or narrow (길이 좁아요).
Both mean dining table. 밥상 is a traditional low dining table (밥상을 차려요), while 식탁 is a modern dining table with chairs (식탁에 앉아요).

ta-27.note: Opposites. 열다 means to open (문을 열어요), while 닫다 means to close (창문을 닫아요).
듣다 means to hear or listen (음악을 들어요), and also means medicine is effective (약이 잘 들어요).
그림 is a drawn or painted artwork (그림을 그려요), while 사진 is a photograph taken with a camera (사진을 찍어요).

ta-28.note: 부르다 means to sing or call (노래를 불러요, 택시를 불러요), and also to feel full after eating (배가 불러요).
찍다 means to take a photo (사진을 찍어요), and also to dip food into sauce (소스를 찍어 먹어요).
Both mean cinema or theater. 극장 also includes live performance stages (극장에서 연극을 봐요), while 영화관 specifically shows movies (영화관에 가요).

ta-29.note: 치다 means to play ball sports with a racket (탁구를 쳐요, 테니스를 쳐요), and also to play piano or clap hands (피아노를 쳐요).
개 means a dog pet (귀여운 개), and also the general counter for everyday items (사과 세 개).
등산 is mountain hiking (주말에 등산을 가요), while 산책 is a gentle walk on level ground (공원에서 산책해요).

ta-30.note: Both mean name. 이름 is standard (이름이 뭐예요?), while 성함 is the respectful honorific word for elders (성함이 어떻게 되세요?).
Both mean person. 사람 is standard (좋은 사람), while 분 is the polite honorific noun and counter (감사한 분, 손님 두 분).
불 means fire (불이 뜨거워요), electric room light (불을 켜요), and also dollars in currency (십 불).

ta-31.note: Opposites. 혼자 means alone or by oneself (혼자 밥을 먹어요), while 함께 means together with others (친구와 함께 공부해요).
Both count people. 명 is standard (학생 세 명), while 분 is the respectful honorific counter (손님 세 분).
Opposites. 남자 means man or male (남자 친구), while 여자 means woman or female (여자 아이).

ta-32.note: Opposites in marriage. 남편 means husband (남편과 산책해요), while 아내 means wife (아내와 식사해요).
Both mean older brother. A male speaker calls his older brother 형, while a female speaker calls him 오빠.
Both mean older sister. A male speaker calls his older sister 누나, while a female speaker calls her 언니.

ta-33.note: 예쁘다 means pretty or cute (꽃이 예뻐요), while 멋있다 means cool, stylish, or handsome (옷이 멋있어요).
Opposites. 선생님 means teacher (선생님께 배워요), while 학생 means student (한국어 반 학생).
살 is the counter for age in years (스무 살), and also means flesh or body weight (살이 빠졌어요).

ta-34.note: Opposites. 배우다 means to learn from someone (한국어를 배워요), while 가르치다 means to teach (학생을 가르쳐요).
쓰다 means to write with a pen (편지를 써요), to wear a hat or use an item (모자를 써요), and to taste bitter (약이 써요).
Opposites. 어렵다 means difficult (시험이 어려워요), while 쉽다 means easy (한국어가 쉬워요).

ta-35.note: 사전 means a dictionary for looking up words (사전을 찾아요), and also means beforehand or in advance (사전 예약).
예 means 'yes' in polite polite speech (예, 알겠습니다), and also an example (예를 들어 설명해요).
Opposites. 합격하다 means to pass a test (시험에 합격했어요), while 불합격하다 means to fail (아쉽게 불합격했어요).

ta-36.note: 한국 means Korea (한국에 살아요), while 외국 means a foreign country outside Korea (외국에 여행 가요).
Both mean country or nation. 나라 is everyday native Korean (어느 나라 사람이에요?), while 국가 is more formal (국가 대표).
영국 means the United Kingdom or Britain (영국 사람), while 미국 means the United States of America (미국 뉴욕).

ta-37.note: Both mean to thank. 고맙다 is warm native Korean (도와줘서 고마워요), while 감사하다 is polite Sino-Korean (진심으로 감사합니다).
Both mean sorry. 미안하다 is used with friends or peers (늦어서 미안해요), while 죄송하다 is more polite for elders (죄송합니다).
Opposites. 네 (or 예) means yes (네, 맞아요), while 아니요 means no (아니요, 아니에요).

ta-38.note: 말 means speech or language (한국 말을 배워요), a horse animal (말을 타요), and also the end of a time period (월말).
Both mean words or speech. 말 is standard (친구의 말), while 말씀 is the respectful honorific word for an elder's speech (선생님 말씀).
Opposites. 알다 means to know (그 사람을 알아요), while 모르다 means not to know (이름을 몰라요).

ta-39.note: 묻다 means to ask a question (길을 물어봐요), to get stained on clothes (옷에 얼룩이 묻어요), and to bury in the ground.
달다 means sweet in taste (초콜릿이 달아요), and also to hang or fasten an item (벽에 시계를 달아요).
보내다 means to send a letter or parcel (편지를 보내요), and also to spend time (주말을 잘 보내요).

ta-40.note: 시청 means city hall building (서울 시청에 가요), and also means watching a television broadcast (뉴스 시청).
Opposites. 질문 means question (질문이 있어요), while 대답 means answer or reply (질문에 대답해요).
Both mean place. 곳 is native Korean (조용한 곳), while 장소 is formal Sino-Korean (약속 장소).

ta-41.note: Opposites. 출발하다 means to depart (기차가 출발해요), while 도착하다 means to arrive (서울역에 도착했어요).
Opposites. 올라가다 means to go up (계단으로 올라가요), while 내려가다 means to go down (아래로 내려가요).
표 means an admission or travel ticket (비행기 표를 사요), and also a chart or table (시간표를 봐요).

ta-42.note: Opposites. 타다 means to get on or ride a vehicle (버스를 타요), while 내리다 means to get off (정류장에서 내려요).
Both mean to look or see. 보다 is general (영화를 봐요), while 구경하다 specifically means to sightsee or browse around (시장을 구경해요).
Both mean to reserve. 예약하다 is used for hotel rooms or restaurants (호텔을 예약해요), while 예매하다 is buying tickets in advance (기차표를 예매해요).

ta-43.note: Opposites. 출근하다 means to go to work in the morning (회사에 출근해요), while 퇴근하다 means to leave work (저녁에 퇴근해요).
일 means work or a task (일을 해요), a calendar day (오늘 며칠이에요?), and the Sino-Korean number one.
역 means a train or subway station (서울역에 가요), and also an acting role in drama (주인공 역).

ta-44.note: Opposites. 입다 (or 신다/쓰다) means to put on clothes, while 벗다 means to take off clothes, shoes, or gloves (장갑을 벗어요).
Opposites. 길다 means long (바지가 길어요), while 짧다 means short (치마가 짧아요).
마르다 means to dry (빨래가 말라요), to feel thirsty (목이 말라요), and to become skinny (몸이 말랐어요).

ta-45.note: 가져오다 means to bring toward the speaker (우산을 가져왔어요), while 가져가다 means to take away (쓰레기를 가져가요).
Both mean to put or place something down. 놓다 (책상 위에 놓아요) and 두다 (가방을 방에 둬요) are often interchangeable.
내다 means to pay money (돈을 내요), to submit an assignment (숙제를 내요), and to make time (시간을 내요).

ta-46.note: 해 means the sun in the sky (해가 밝아요), and also a calendar year (새해 복 많이 받으세요).
Opposites for temperature of things. 차갑다 means cold to touch (차가운 물), while 뜨겁다 means hot (뜨거운 차).
Opposites. 편하다 means comfortable or convenient (신발이 편해요), while 불편하다 means uncomfortable (자리가 불편해요).

ta-47.note: 새 means a flying bird (새가 노래해요), and also means new placed before a noun (새 옷을 입어요).
달리다 means to run fast (운동장을 달려요), and also to hang or dangle (나무에 열매가 달렸어요).
개 refers to a fully grown dog (큰 개), while 강아지 specifically refers to a young puppy or cute small dog (귀여운 강아지).

ta-48.note: 차 means an automobile or car (차를 운전해요), and also a tea drink (따뜻한 차를 마셔요).
Both mean age. 나이 is standard (나이가 몇 살이에요?), while 연세 is the respectful honorific word for elders (할머니 연세).
Opposites. 아이 means a child (아이가 웃어요), while 어른 means an adult (어른에게 인사해요).
